methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/FM.json), cross-checked against derived/scope_packets/FM.json source_quality.unresolved_headings (2 entries: Acronyms, Antimicrobial/Antiviral/Antifungal Quick Reference) and body-page OCR (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/) for both the unresolved headings and the structurally distinct merged_duplicate_headings recorded on FM.S05 (Complementary and Integrative Medicine) and FM.S06 (References). Both unresolved headings were independently resolved via body-heading confirmation: Acronyms opens page FM2 (pdf 378) immediately before Four Principles of Family Medicine (folded into SU-FM-01, node id UNCATALOGUED:FM.ACRONYMS); Antimicrobial/Antiviral/Antifungal Quick Reference spans FM54-FM55 (pdf 430-431), between the Palliative Care section and Landmark Family Medicine Trials (its own unit, SU-FM-56, node id UNCATALOGUED:FM.ANTIMICROBIAL_REF). Complementary and Integrative Medicine (FM53, pdf 429) is a genuine distinct topic (Table 25, herbal products) absorbed into the FM.S05 node by TOC extraction rather than given its own node_id; represented as its own unit (SU-FM-55, node id UNCATALOGUED:FM.CAM) rather than folded into the Palliative Care units, since its content (herbal-product safety) is unrelated to palliative care. Unlike prior chapters, FM required no line-wrap or two-column TOC merge repair beyond these three items; all 37 Common Presenting Problems and 5 screening-guideline topics were confirmed unmerged, one TOC node per named topic. Per the FM-specific instruction that Family Medicine is cross-cutting, every study unit whose topic is also covered by a completed or not-yet-mapped chapter carries a cross_discipline_note in crosswalk.json documenting the overlap and the distinguishing FM angle (undifferentiated/primary-care presentation, longitudinal management, or preventive/counselling context) for the later global chapter-overlap audit; only Power of Attorney/Instructional Advance Directives (SU-FM-53) was judged thin enough relative to its already-completed ELOM-chapter counterpart to classify CROSS_DISCIPLINE rather than DIRECT/COMPONENT.

organizational_header_nodes.FM: Chapter root container - represented by all study units below.
organizational_header_nodes.FM.S02: 'Periodic Health Examination' umbrella heading (FM3); carries no independent content beyond its seven T-children (Purpose of the PHE, GRADE Classification, and five cancer-screening-guideline topics), each represented as its own study unit (SU-FM-02 through SU-FM-07).
organizational_header_nodes.FM.S03: 'Health Promotion and Counselling' umbrella heading (FM7); carries no independent content beyond its seven T-children, each represented as its own study unit (SU-FM-08 through SU-FM-14).
organizational_header_nodes.FM.S04: 'Common Presenting Problems' umbrella heading (FM16); carries no independent content beyond its thirty-seven T-children, each a distinct named primary-care presenting complaint represented as its own study unit (SU-FM-15 through SU-FM-51).

study_units.title: Acronyms and Four Principles of Family Medicine
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Acromyms' (raw OCR, trailing page-number digits did not parse to a trusted anchor - listed as unresolved in derived/scope_packets/FM.json source_quality.unresolved_headings) is confirmed via body-heading OCR (clean-ocr/0378.txt, pdf 378) to be the acronym glossary table occupying the top of page FM2, immediately followed on the same page by the 'Four Principles of Family Medicine' section (FM.S01, College of Family Physicians of Canada four principles + 'Experts in Generalism' text). No toc_inventory.json node_id exists for the Acronyms heading; recorded as UNCATALOGUED:FM.ACRONYMS per the documented convention for a heading with no canonical node. Combined into one unit: pure glossary plus foundational professional-identity content, both non-disease background for the chapter.

study_units.title: Purpose of the Periodic Health Examination and Classification of Recommendations (GRADE)
study_units.structural_rationale: Two adjacent TOC topic nodes under 'Periodic Health Examination' (FM.S02); both are methodology/framework content (why a PHE is done; how the GRADE strength-of-recommendation system is used to grade the screening guidelines that follow) rather than a distinct clinical presentation, consolidated into one unit rather than given independent testable-competency status like the disease-specific screening topics that follow.

study_units.title: Principles of Palliative Care and End-of-Life Care Discussions
study_units.structural_rationale: Two adjacent TOC topic nodes under Palliative Care (FM.S05), both confirmed via body OCR (clean-ocr/0428.txt, pdf 428) as the opening principles-of-palliative-care content and the associated end-of-life goals-of-care conversation guidance on the same page; consolidated as one communication/philosophy-of-care unit distinct from the procedural/legal Power of Attorney and Advance Directives units that follow.

study_units.title: Power of Attorney and Instructional Advance Directives
study_units.structural_rationale: Two adjacent TOC topic nodes under Palliative Care (FM.S05) covering the legal/documentation mechanisms of substitute decision-making (Power of Attorney for personal care) and instructional advance directives; consolidated as one unit since both are the same legal-planning competency (who decides, and what they are bound by) rather than two distinct clinical presentations.

study_units.title: Symptom Management in Palliative Care
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC topic node under Palliative Care (FM.S05) covering pharmacologic/nonpharmacologic management of common end-of-life symptoms (pain, dyspnea, nausea, delirium). The parent FM.S05 section node itself (page range FM52-FM55) is also referenced here for the portion of its span not covered by any other T-child or by the Complementary/Integrative-Medicine and Antimicrobial-Reference units below.

study_units.title: Complementary and Integrative Medicine (Common Herbal Products)
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Complementary and Integrative Medicine' is recorded in toc_inventory.json as a merged_duplicate_heading absorbed into the FM.S05 (Palliative Care) section node rather than given its own node_id, because it sits within FM.S05's page span (FM52-FM55) but is a structurally distinct topic (Table 25, 'Common Herbal Products': reported uses, adverse effects, and drug interactions of common natural health products) unrelated to palliative care, confirmed via body OCR (clean-ocr/0429.txt, pdf 429). No standalone toc_inventory.json node_id exists for it; recorded as UNCATALOGUED:FM.CAM per the documented convention.

study_units.title: Antimicrobial/Antiviral/Antifungal Quick Reference
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC heading 'Antimicrobial/Antiviral/Antifungal Quick Reference' (raw OCR, trailing page-number digits did not parse to a trusted anchor - listed as unresolved in derived/scope_packets/FM.json source_quality.unresolved_headings) is confirmed via body-heading OCR (clean-ocr/0430.txt and clean-ocr/0431.txt, pdf 430-431) as a two-page condition-by-microorganism-by-empiric-therapy reference table (respiratory/ENT and dermatologic conditions), positioned between the Palliative Care section (ending FM55) and Landmark Family Medicine Trials (starting FM56). No toc_inventory.json node_id exists for it; recorded as UNCATALOGUED:FM.ANTIMICROBIAL_REF per the documented convention.

study_units.title: Landmark Family Medicine Trials and References
study_units.structural_rationale: TOC section node 'Landmark Family Medicine Trials' (FM.S06), with toc_inventory.json recording 'References' as a merged_duplicate_heading absorbed into the same node (the References list immediately follows the landmark-trials table with no independent subheading of its own). Pure bibliographic/evidence-summary appendix content.
